blocks.text: Release overview

macOS Sonoma 14.0 was released publicly on September 26, 2023. Its launch feature set emphasized desktop personalization, video conferencing, browsing, and gaming, with interactive desktop widgets, screen savers that become wallpaper, Presenter Overlay, Safari profiles and web apps, and Game Mode.

citations.locator: Availability; Widgets and Stunning Screen Savers; Powerful Productivity for Video Conferencing; Enhanced Browsing with Safari; An Immersive Gaming Experience

blocks.text: Administration and development

Sonoma also expanded managed-device capabilities. Apple documents date-and-time enforcement for software updates, account-driven enrollment, Managed Device Attestation, new certificate declarations, network relays, and hardware-bound ACME keys. The corresponding SDK notes collect the platform's framework-level additions, behavior changes, and resolved issues for developers.
Release overview

watchOS 10.0 reached the public channel on September 18, 2023. The release redesigned many built-in apps, added the context-aware Smart Stack and new navigation conventions, introduced five watch faces, and substantially expanded cycling, hiking, mental-health, and daylight-tracking tools.

citations.locator: September 18, 2023; New Design Language and Navigation; New Watch Faces

blocks.text: Release boundaries

Apple's launch article separately marked NameDrop, additional Smart Stack media suggestions, and Fitness+ Audio Focus for updates later in 2023, so those features are not attributed to the 10.0 public appearance here. Mobile Device Management support, by contrast, was identified as part of watchOS 10 at launch.
Release overview

tvOS 17.0 became publicly available on September 18, 2023. FaceTime arrived on supported Apple TV 4K models through Continuity Camera, while Control Center, Siri Remote discovery, Apple Music Sing, Memories screen savers, Siri, and dialogue enhancement broadened the living-room experience.

citations.locator: September 18, 2023; Additional features available with tvOS 17

blocks.text: Developer scope

The tvOS 17 SDK added developer-facing capabilities including StoreKit 2 merchandising views and subscription-status APIs, along with scrolling, selection, and sector marks in Swift Charts. Webex and Zoom television apps were announced for later in 2023 and are therefore outside this 17.0 launch record.

citations.locator: StoreKit — New Features; Swift Charts — New Features

blocks.text: Release overview

visionOS 1.0 was the launch operating system for Apple Vision Pro when the device became available in the United States on February 2, 2024. It introduced a three-dimensional interface controlled with eyes, hands, and voice, an unbounded workspace for scalable app windows, immersive Environments, and a dedicated App Store alongside compatible iPhone and iPad apps.

citations.locator: Pricing and Availability; A Revolutionary Operating System and User Interface; Extraordinary Experiences

blocks.text: Privacy and accessibility

The initial platform paired Optic ID with private eye-tracking behavior and a visible capture indicator in EyeSight. Its spatial accessibility set included adaptations of VoiceOver, Zoom, Switch Control, and Guided Access, plus Pointer Control, Dwell Control, Voice Control, and dominant-eye tracking.

citations.locator: Privacy and Security at Its Core; Accessibility in visionOS

blocks.text: Release overview

visionOS 1.1 was released on March 7, 2024. It established the platform's first enterprise-management toolset, added Contact Key Verification, improved Persona and EyeSight rendering, refined the virtual keyboard and Mac Virtual Display, and enabled setup on captive Wi-Fi networks.
Developer and security record

Apple's SDK notes document closer placement for volumetric scenes, immersive-space coordinate APIs, StoreKit transaction metadata, and fixes affecting app upgrades, passcodes, passkeys, Siri, and spatial UI. The security advisory covers notification spoofing, image parsing, kernel protections, Persona access, Safari, and WebKit.

citations.locator: App Placement; General; Lock Screen; Passcode; Passkeys; Siri; StoreKit; SwiftUI

blocks.text: Release overview

visionOS 1.2 was released on June 10, 2024. Apple described the update as adding regional and language support, bug fixes, and security updates; that localization work prepared Vision Pro for availability later in June and July across nine additional countries and regions.

citations.locator: Pricing and Availability — Vision Pro comes with visionOS 1.2

blocks.text: Resolved issues and security

The SDK notes list targeted fixes for recent-call synchronization, the mini keyboard's emoji keyplane, and App Store review-request presentation in compatible iPhone and iPad apps. Apple's security advisory records fixes across media processing, storage and privilege boundaries, the kernel, Safari permissions, and WebKit.
Release overview

visionOS 1.3 was released on July 29, 2024 as a maintenance and security update. Apple Support did not enumerate consumer features, and the developer page explicitly says there were no new release notes for the software update.

citations.locator: General — There are no new release notes for this software update

blocks.text: Documented security work

The security record is the substantive first-party detail for this release. It covers AirDrop quarantine handling, media and image processing, kernel information and network protections, Persona behavior while the virtual keyboard is active, Shortcuts internet permission checks, and WebKit failures and content restrictions.

citations.locator: AirDrop; Apple Neural Engine; AppleAVD; CoreGraphics; ImageIO; Kernel; Presence; Shortcuts; WebKit

events.summary: macOS Sonoma 14.0 reached the public release channel on September 26, 2023 with desktop widgets and screen savers, new conferencing and Safari workflows, Game Mode, and expanded administration controls.

blocks.text: Public release

Apple made macOS Sonoma available on September 26, 2023. This record describes that public appearance; it does not project the cumulative Sonoma feature list backward onto any developer or public beta milestone.
What changed

The public release combined desktop customization, richer video calls, separated Safari browsing contexts, app-like websites, gaming prioritization on Apple silicon, and new managed-device controls. Hardware, regional, and app support qualifications still applied to individual features.

changes.title: Interactive desktop and iPhone widgets
changes.canonicalSummary: Widgets can be placed directly on the Mac desktop, perform supported actions, and include nearby iPhone widgets through Continuity.
changes.summary: Sonoma added interactive desktop widgets that visually recede behind active apps and can surface compatible widgets from a nearby iPhone.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Screen savers that become wallpaper
changes.canonicalSummary: New location-based screen savers transition into matching desktop wallpaper after the user signs in.
changes.summary: The release introduced slow-motion location screen savers and a transition that carries the selected scene onto the desktop.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Presenter Overlay and gesture reactions
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported Macs can place the presenter over shared content and trigger three-dimensional call reactions with gestures.
changes.summary: Video-conferencing apps gained a system presentation layer and gesture-triggered effects, subject to Apple-silicon and Continuity Camera requirements.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Safari profiles, web apps, and private browsing protections
changes.canonicalSummary: Safari separates work and personal contexts with profiles, turns sites into Dock-based web apps, and strengthens private-window protections.
changes.summary: Browsing gained isolated profiles, app-like website launchers, locked private windows, tracker blocking, and URL tracking-parameter removal.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Game Mode on Apple silicon
changes.canonicalSummary: Game Mode gives a running game higher CPU and GPU priority while reducing latency for supported wireless controllers and AirPods.
changes.summary: Supported Apple-silicon Macs gained a game-focused scheduling mode intended to stabilize frame rates and reduce controller and audio latency.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Declarative updates and account-driven enrollment
changes.canonicalSummary: Managed Macs gained deadline-based software-update enforcement, account-driven enrollment, attestation, and additional certificate and network declarations.
changes.summary: Sonoma expanded device administration with enforceable update dates, new enrollment paths, Managed Device Attestation, and broader declarative configuration.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's enterprise documentation to the audited public release.

events.summary: watchOS 10.0 reached the public release channel on September 18, 2023 with a redesigned app experience, Smart Stack, new faces, richer cycling and hiking tools, well-being features, and MDM support.

blocks.text: Public release
Apple released watchOS 10 on September 18, 2023 for Apple Watch Series 4 and later paired with a compatible iPhone running iOS 17. This article records the public appearance only.
What changed

The release reworked navigation and information density, added new faces and major outdoor-workout capabilities, expanded mental and physical well-being tools, and introduced centralized enterprise management. Features that Apple expressly scheduled for later updates, including NameDrop, are excluded from this 10.0 occurrence set.

changes.title: Redesigned apps, Smart Stack, and navigation
changes.canonicalSummary: Built-in apps use more of the watch display, contextual widgets appear in a Smart Stack, and hardware buttons adopt new navigation roles.
changes.summary: watchOS redesigned many apps for glanceability, exposed contextual widgets through the Digital Crown, moved Control Center to the side button, and added recent-app switching.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Five new watch faces
changes.canonicalSummary: Snoopy, Palette, Solar Analog, Nike Globe, and Modular Ultra broaden the face catalog, with Modular Ultra limited to Apple Watch Ultra.
changes.summary: The public release introduced five faces spanning animated characters, color, solar position, Nike styling, and an information-dense Ultra layout.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Cycling sensors, Power Zones, and iPhone Live Activity
changes.canonicalSummary: Cycling workouts connect to Bluetooth power, speed, and cadence sensors, calculate new metrics, and present workout views on a paired iPhone.
changes.summary: Cyclists gained external-sensor support, wattage and cadence data, Functional Threshold Power zones, speed views, and a handlebar-friendly iPhone presentation.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Expanded Compass and Maps tools for outdoor use
changes.canonicalSummary: Compass adds connection and emergency waypoints plus elevation views, while Maps brings supported offline and topographic information to the watch.
changes.summary: Outdoor navigation gained cellular and emergency reference points, waypoint elevation, offline routes from a paired iPhone, and U.S. park topographic and trail details.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: State of Mind logging and time in daylight
changes.canonicalSummary: Mindfulness can record momentary emotions or daily moods, and supported watches measure time spent in daylight using the ambient light sensor.
changes.summary: watchOS added structured mood reflection with contributing factors and reminders, plus daylight-duration measurement on supported models.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

citations.locator: watchOS 10 — Mindfulness; Other features and improvements — Time in Daylight

changes.title: Mobile Device Management for Apple Watch
changes.canonicalSummary: Enterprise administrators can centrally install apps and configure accounts, passcodes, Wi-Fi, and VPN settings on managed Apple Watch fleets.
changes.summary: watchOS 10 introduced MDM support for remote application deployment and configuration of core account, network, and passcode settings.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's launch-day enterprise description to the audited public release.

events.summary: tvOS 17.0 reached the public release channel on September 18, 2023 with FaceTime through Continuity Camera, a redesigned Control Center, remote finding, new music and photo experiences, and clearer dialogue.

blocks.text: Public release

Apple made tvOS 17 available on September 18, 2023 as a free update for Apple TV 4K and Apple TV HD. FaceTime required Apple TV 4K (2nd generation or later), and other features carried their own hardware, subscription, language, or regional limits.
What changed

The launch release connected iPhone or iPad cameras to television calls, reorganized system controls, helped locate newer Siri Remotes, and expanded music, photo, Siri, and dialogue workflows. Webex and Zoom apps were announced for later in the year and are not counted as 17.0 changes.

citations.locator: Later this year; Additional features available with tvOS 17

changes.title: FaceTime with Continuity Camera
changes.canonicalSummary: Supported Apple TV 4K models use a nearby iPhone or iPad camera and microphone for FaceTime calls on the television.
changes.summary: Users could start FaceTime on Apple TV or hand off a call from another device, with Center Stage, reactions, and shared viewing on supported hardware.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

changes.title: Redesigned Control Center
changes.canonicalSummary: Control Center presents time, active profile, system status, and context-sensitive settings in a reorganized television interface.
changes.summary: The system-control overlay was redesigned to expose current status and relevant controls more directly from the Home Screen.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

citations.locator: Additional features available with tvOS 17 — redesigned Control Center

changes.title: Siri Remote locator on iPhone
changes.canonicalSummary: The Apple TV Remote interface on iPhone guides a user toward a nearby Siri Remote (2nd generation or later).
changes.summary: A proximity-style onscreen guide in iPhone Control Center helps find supported misplaced Siri Remotes.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

citations.locator: Additional features available with tvOS 17 — Siri Remote locator

changes.title: Apple Music Sing with Continuity Camera
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Music Sing can place the singer's camera image and effects on screen through Continuity Camera on supported hardware.
changes.summary: Apple TV 4K (3rd generation) gained an on-screen camera performance mode for Apple Music Sing, with an Apple Music subscription required.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's dated availability announcement and its hardware footnote to the audited public release.

citations.locator: Additional features available with tvOS 17 — Apple Music Sing; footnote 2

changes.title: Memories as screen savers
changes.canonicalSummary: Curated Memories from a personal or shared photo library can become Apple TV screen savers.
changes.summary: The screen-saver picker gained photo-library Memories assembled from a user's own library, Shared Library, or both.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

citations.locator: Additional features available with tvOS 17 — Memories as screen savers

changes.title: Enhance Dialogue with HomePod (2nd generation)
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple TV 4K paired with HomePod (2nd generation) can emphasize speech over effects, action, and music.
changes.summary: The audio mix gained a speech-forward option that separated dialogue from background sound and brought it toward the center channel.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's dated availability announcement to the audited public release.

citations.locator: Additional features available with tvOS 17 — Enhance Dialogue

events.summary: visionOS 1.0 reached its public appearance with the U.S. launch of Apple Vision Pro on February 2, 2024, introducing Apple's spatial interface, scalable app workspace, Environments, app catalog, privacy controls, and accessibility system.

blocks.text: Public release

visionOS 1.0 was the shipping platform when Apple Vision Pro became available in the United States on February 2, 2024. The date in this record is the product's public availability date, not the January announcement date.

citations.locator: Pricing and Availability — availability beginning Friday, February 2

blocks.text: What changed

The first public visionOS release established eye, hand, and voice input; windows unconstrained by a physical display; immersive environments; native and compatible app distribution; iris authentication and private eye tracking; and spatial adaptations of Apple's accessibility tools.

citations.locator: A Revolutionary Operating System and User Interface; Extraordinary Experiences; Privacy and Security at Its Core; Accessibility in visionOS

changes.title: Three-dimensional interface with eye, hand, and voice input
changes.canonicalSummary: visionOS presents spatial controls and content that users target with their eyes, select with hand gestures, and operate with voice, keyboards, or dictation.
changes.summary: The launch platform established looking, pinching, wrist scrolling, virtual typing, dictation, and Siri as its core interaction system.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's Vision Pro availability announcement to the audited public appearance.

citations.locator: A Revolutionary Operating System and User Interface

changes.title: Scalable app windows on an infinite canvas
changes.canonicalSummary: Apps can be arranged side by side, moved through the user's space, and scaled beyond the bounds of a conventional display.
changes.summary: visionOS 1.0 introduced a multitasking workspace in which multiple app windows could occupy and scale within the surrounding environment.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's Vision Pro availability announcement to the audited public appearance.

citations.locator: visionOS 1.0 — three-dimensional interface and infinite canvas
Extraordinary Experiences — infinite canvas for productivity

changes.title: Immersive Environments
changes.canonicalSummary: Dynamic spatial landscapes can partially or fully replace the visible room, with immersion controlled through the Digital Crown.
changes.summary: The initial release included environmental scenes designed to reduce visual clutter or immerse the wearer beyond the physical room.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's Vision Pro availability announcement to the audited public appearance.

citations.locator: A Revolutionary Operating System and User Interface — Environments

changes.title: visionOS App Store and compatible iPhone and iPad apps
changes.canonicalSummary: A dedicated App Store distributes spatial experiences while more than one million compatible iOS and iPadOS apps work with the new input system.
changes.summary: At launch, Vision Pro combined apps designed for spatial computing with a large catalog of compatible iPhone and iPad applications.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple Support and Apple's Vision Pro availability announcement to the audited public appearance.

citations.locator: visionOS 1.0 — App Store and compatible apps

changes.title: Optic ID and eye-tracking privacy
changes.canonicalSummary: Optic ID authenticates with the iris, gaze data remains private from Apple and apps, and EyeSight indicates spatial capture to nearby people.
changes.summary: The launch security model added iris-based unlocking, payment and password authorization, protected gaze information, and an outward capture indicator.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's Vision Pro availability announcement to the audited public appearance.

citations.locator: Privacy and Security at Its Core

changes.title: Spatial accessibility controls
changes.canonicalSummary: visionOS adapts VoiceOver, Zoom, Switch Control, and Guided Access while adding spatial Pointer, Dwell, Voice Control, and dominant-eye options.
changes.summary: Users could combine eyes, hands, voice, finger, or wrist input, pause to select items, and use one dominant eye for tracking when needed.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's Vision Pro availability announcement to the audited public appearance.

events.summary: visionOS 1.1 reached the public release channel on March 7, 2024 with enterprise management, Contact Key Verification, Persona and accessibility improvements, keyboard and Mac display fixes, and captive-network setup.

blocks.text: Public release

Apple's security release record dates visionOS 1.1 to March 7, 2024. The cumulative visionOS update page assigns the product and workflow changes below to the 1.1 section, so none are inferred from beta notes.
What changed

The update made Vision Pro manageable in enterprise fleets, added identity-verification and immersive-captioning support, refined Persona and EyeSight, corrected several keyboard and Mac Virtual Display failures, and enabled activation through captive Wi-Fi portals.

citations.locator: visionOS 1.1 — Mobile Device Management; Messages; Accessibility; Persona (beta) and EyeSight; Virtual keyboard; Mac Virtual Display; Captive Network Support

changes.title: Enterprise Mobile Device Management
changes.canonicalSummary: visionOS gained account-driven enrollment, managed network and account configuration, volume app deployment, remote erase, and device inventory.
changes.summary: Organizations could enroll Vision Pro with Managed Apple IDs, configure Wi-Fi, VPN, email and SSO, deploy apps at scale, inventory devices, and erase them remotely.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's version-labeled update notes to the audited public release and its dated security record.

changes.title: iMessage Contact Key Verification
changes.canonicalSummary: Messages gained Contact Key Verification for users who need additional assurance about the identity of their conversation partners.
changes.summary: The release brought Apple's high-assurance iMessage contact-verification capability to Vision Pro.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's version-labeled update notes to the audited public release.

changes.title: Anchored captions for Apple Immersive Video
changes.canonicalSummary: Closed captions can be anchored to playback controls while a user watches Apple Immersive Video.
changes.summary: Immersive playback gained a stable caption placement option tied to the media-control area.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's version-labeled update notes to the audited public release.

changes.title: Persona and EyeSight improvements
changes.canonicalSummary: Persona enrollment can run hands-free, facial rendering is refined, and EyeSight improves its representation of the wearer's eyes.
changes.summary: The beta Persona system added hands-free capture and updated hair, makeup, neck, mouth, and eye rendering, while EyeSight improved eye appearance.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's version-labeled update notes to the audited public release.

changes.title: Virtual keyboard accuracy and placement fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Text cursor placement is more accurate, and fixes address keyboard obstruction, preview synchronization, and unexpected edit menus.
changes.summary: Apple corrected four documented text-entry problems involving cursor targeting, keyboard position, preview synchronization, and edit-menu presentation.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's version-labeled update notes to the audited public release.

changes.title: Mac Virtual Display connectivity fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Mac discovery and connection become more reliable, with fixes for Universal Control interruption and missing paired Bluetooth devices.
changes.summary: The update resolved documented failures around finding a Mac, maintaining Universal Control, and reconnecting when a paired Bluetooth accessory was unavailable.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's version-labeled update notes to the audited public release.

changes.title: Setup on captive Wi-Fi networks
changes.canonicalSummary: Apple Vision Pro can be set up while connected to a network that requires a web-based captive-portal sign-in.
changes.summary: Initial device setup became possible on hotel, cafe, airport, and similar Wi-Fi networks with captive login pages.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's version-labeled update notes to the audited public release.

events.summary: visionOS 1.2 reached the public release channel on June 10, 2024 with regional and language readiness for international expansion, three documented workflow fixes, and broad system, media, Safari, and WebKit security repairs.

blocks.text: Public release

Apple's security advisory dates visionOS 1.2 to June 10, 2024. The same day's international announcement says Vision Pro would ship with 1.2 and language support in newly served countries and regions; device sales there began later, on June 28 or July 12.
What changed

The compact feature record consists of localization support and fixes for FaceTime recent-call synchronization, the mini keyboard's emoji view, and App Store review UI in compatible apps. Apple's advisory supplies the larger technical record across media, kernel, privilege, browser, and web-content boundaries.

changes.title: Additional region and language support
changes.canonicalSummary: visionOS added localization needed for Vision Pro's expansion beyond the United States into nine further countries and regions.
changes.summary: The update prepared Vision Pro for later June and July launches in China mainland, Hong Kong, Japan, Singapore, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, and the United Kingdom.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's version-labeled update note, dated release advisory, and international availability announcement.

citations.locator: Pricing and Availability — Vision Pro comes with visionOS 1.2

changes.title: FaceTime recent-call synchronization
changes.canonicalSummary: Recent calls now synchronize between Vision Pro and a user's iPhone, iPad, or Apple Watch.
changes.summary: The SDK notes mark the cross-device recent-call history failure as resolved in visionOS 1.2.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's final SDK release note to the audited public release.

changes.title: Mini keyboard emoji keyplane fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Opening emoji from the mini keyboard now presents the intended emoji keyplane instead of redirecting to a letter layout.
changes.summary: Apple corrected a keyboard-layout error that displayed a letter keyplane and extra platter space when the user selected emoji.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's final SDK release note to the audited public release.

changes.title: App Store review-request UI fix
changes.canonicalSummary: Review-request interfaces render correctly when a compatible iPhone or iPad app is tested or run on visionOS.
changes.summary: The release corrected malformed presentation from App Store review APIs inside compatible iOS and iPadOS apps.
changes.verificationMethod: Matched Apple's final SDK release note to the audited public release.

changes.title: System, media, and privilege security fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Security updates address code execution, memory handling, privilege elevation, and data-access risks across media, image, storage, Metal, and kernel components.
changes.summary: Apple's advisory groups fixes under AVEVideoEncoder, CoreMedia, Disk Images, Foundation, ImageIO, IOSurface, Kernel, libiconv, Metal, Messages, and Transparency.
changes.verificationMethod: Summarized affected components and impact classes from Apple's version-specific security advisory.

changes.title: Safari and WebKit security fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Browser fixes address persistent permission dialogs, code execution, fingerprinting, denial of service, and web-content processing failures.
changes.summary: The release tightened Safari permission handling and resolved multiple WebKit, Canvas, and Web Inspector vulnerabilities documented by Apple.
changes.verificationMethod: Summarized affected components and impact classes from Apple's version-specific security advisory.

citations.locator: visionOS 1.2 — Safari; WebKit; WebKit Canvas; WebKit Web Inspector

events.summary: visionOS 1.3 reached the public release channel on July 29, 2024 as a maintenance and security release, with no separately enumerated developer features and a detailed advisory covering AirDrop, media, kernel, Persona, Shortcuts, and WebKit.

blocks.text: Public release

Apple's security record dates visionOS 1.3 to July 29, 2024. Apple Support characterizes it as bug fixes and security updates, while the developer release-note page says there are no new release notes for this software update.

citations.locator: General — There are no new release notes for this software update

blocks.text: What is documented

Because Apple did not enumerate consumer or SDK features, this occurrence set stays within the version-specific security advisory. The grouped entries below summarize affected surfaces and impact classes without turning later advisory revisions into claims about a separate release.

changes.title: AirDrop quarantine-flag handling
changes.canonicalSummary: Files received through AirDrop now receive the expected quarantine flag after Apple corrected the related state handling.
changes.summary: The advisory records a fix for an AirDrop path in which a received file could lack its quarantine marker.
changes.verificationMethod: Summarized the affected component and impact from Apple's version-specific security advisory.

changes.title: Media and image-processing security fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: Memory and input-validation fixes reduce termination and denial-of-service risks in Apple Neural Engine, AppleAVD, CoreGraphics, and ImageIO.
changes.summary: Apple documented hardening for neural, video, graphics, and image-processing paths that could otherwise crash the system or an application.
changes.verificationMethod: Summarized affected components and impact classes from Apple's version-specific security advisory.

citations.locator: visionOS 1.3 — Apple Neural Engine; AppleAVD; CoreGraphics; ImageIO

changes.title: Kernel information, network, and stability protections
changes.canonicalSummary: Kernel fixes address memory-layout disclosure, network-packet spoofing from a privileged position, and local unexpected shutdown.
changes.summary: The update improved private-data redaction, locking, and memory handling across three kernel vulnerabilities documented by Apple.
changes.verificationMethod: Summarized affected components and impact classes from Apple's version-specific security advisory.

changes.title: Persona suspension during virtual-keyboard use
changes.canonicalSummary: The system suspends Persona while the virtual keyboard is active to prevent keyboard input from being inferred from the representation.
changes.summary: Apple changed Persona behavior during text entry to close a side channel that could reveal virtual-keyboard input.
changes.verificationMethod: Summarized the affected component, impact, and remediation from Apple's version-specific security advisory.

changes.title: Shortcuts internet-permission checks
changes.canonicalSummary: Additional logic checks prevent a shortcut from bypassing internet-access permission requirements.
changes.summary: The Shortcuts runtime tightened permission enforcement for actions that attempt to reach the internet.
changes.verificationMethod: Summarized the affected component and impact from Apple's version-specific security advisory.

changes.title: WebKit crash, scripting, and restriction fixes
changes.canonicalSummary: WebKit fixes address denial of service, process crashes, cross-site scripting, and bypass of certain web-content restrictions.
changes.summary: Apple's advisory lists memory, bounds, validation, and URL-protocol changes across multiple web-content vulnerabilities.
changes.verificationMethod: Summarized affected components and impact classes from Apple's version-specific security advisory.
